reviews.verification: Cancellation requires common factors and preserves all original denominator exclusions; rearranging an identity differs from solving an equation.
Factorisation/quadratic formula agree, both signs retained; for ax²+bx+c the root sum is -b/a and product c/a when a is nonzero.
Completing the square preserves the leading coefficient; discriminant cases require a genuine quadratic, with a=0 checked separately.
Zeros and poles partition sign intervals; strict and non-strict endpoints differ, and multiplying by an unknown-sign expression is not automatically valid.
Positive-base index laws are valid; equating exponents additionally needs the common base to differ from1. Corrected that missing qualification.
Product/quotient/power log rules are used only for positive arguments and valid bases; transformed candidates retain the original domain.
Optimisation on the actual inner range must check an admissible vertex, endpoints and unattained boundaries; positive reciprocals reverse order.
An inclusive AP block has last-index minus first-index plus1 terms; symmetric pairs share the average of its endpoints and partial-sum subtraction isolates it.
Finite GP formula needs a separate r=1 case; infinite convergence requires |r|<1. Filtering an event does not silently change an unconditional sample-space denominator.
Term-position equations for AP and GP precede elimination; an infinite-sum formula is used only after checking the resulting ratio.
Every product term chooses exactly one summand from each bracket; target powers must sum correctly and each choice includes its numerical coefficient.
An input transformation is inverted when tracking points; an output transformation acts on heights. Negative output scale exchanges maxima and minima.
Completed squares give centre coordinates with reversed inner signs and squared radius; radius² positive, zero or negative gives a circle, point or no real locus.
Conditional probabilities restrict the sample space; without-replacement counts change at each draw. Routes multiply conditionally and disjoint routes add.
Sine/cosine period2pi, tangent periodpi, their stated domains/ranges, exact values and even/odd symmetries are correct; input scaling applies to the whole angle.
Trig identities do not remove domain restrictions; dividing may lose zero-factor cases, and squaring needs original sign checks including sqrt(a²)=|a|.
Sine/cosine rules require the indicated sides/angles; SSA may yield two triangles and needs nondegeneracy and angle-sum checks. Area uses the included angle.
Termwise rational-power differentiation is valid on the expression domain; a second derivative requires differentiating twice before substituting.
Stationary roots and domain breaks delimit sign tests. A derivative zero alone is insufficient for an extremum, and its height comes from the original function.
The power antiderivative excludes exponent-1; endpoint subtraction has the correct order. Added that an initial value determines the constant only on its own connected interval.
Geometric area integrates upper minus lower separately on each region; an ordinary definite integral is signed and may cancel across crossings.
Ratios become equations without dropping denominator restrictions. Exponential substitutions are positive and monotonicity is used only for a valid base.
Lengths are nonnegative, so square roots of squares require absolute values until the geometric domain fixes the sign; triangle-area ratios retain included-angle factors.
Binomial coefficients include combination and both numerical power factors. Prime divisibility arguments check endpoints and all factors, not just n choose k.
Trig root counts retain both branches and the transformed interval; tangent poles and zero divisors are excluded and duplicate endpoint solutions count once.
For a>0, a^cosx ranges between a and1/a; separation is |a-1/a|. Vertex/endpoints and sign-compatible roots determine attainable extrema.
Circle separation uses centre distances and radii; unspecified right angles need cases. Negative-reciprocal gradients exclude horizontal/vertical special cases.
Circle areas depend on radius squared; differences of quadratic radii can form an AP, with the exact band count checked before summing.
Distance minimisation uses both coordinate differences; squaring is order-preserving for nonnegative distances. A squared substitution keeps its nonnegative domain.
A common height gives a side-area ratio; the cosine-rule quadratic can encode both SSA triangles. Height/adjacent-side comparisons need an acute stated angle.
Tangent gradient is f-prime at the contact point; a zero tangent gradient gives a vertical normal. Parameters stay fixed during differentiation.
A substitution names the entire repeated expression, preserves its image/range, and must be inverted at the end; coefficient ratios retain binomial factors.
Monotone intervals and turning heights determine crossing counts. Touching roots are counted once, and counting positive roots also requires the value/boundary at zero.
Sine symmetry inputs are pi/2+kpi and cosine symmetry inputs kpi. Corrected the period statement to nonconstant sine/cosine with nonzero input coefficient, rather than all trig graphs.
Totals equal means times counts; pooled means are weighted. Swaps conserve combined totals while removals change counts, and percentages translate to amounts.
Reflection in y=k sends y to2k-y; vertical shifts add signed rectangles, while overlapping integral intervals may count a region more than once.

A repeated single value forces future repetition only for an autonomous one-term recurrence. Corrected the statement to require full state/index phase for other recurrences; cycles and leftover terms then sum correctly.
Square-factor extraction and conjugate multiplication are valid with a nonzero denominator; sqrt(x²) remains |x| and original exclusions survive simplification.
Polynomial division stops below divisor degree. Substitution at a linear divisor zero gives its constant remainder; a zero remainder is the factor case.
Circle-angle theorems refer to the correct chord/arc; a tangent radius and centre-to-chord perpendicular produce right triangles. Internal/external contact need distinct cases.
Arc/sector formulas use radians; a segment subtracts the correct triangle and a perimeter includes all exposed arcs and radial edges.
Displacements are finish minus start; transformations use the specified centre and order. Negative scale reverses directions while area/volume scale by square/cube magnitudes as appropriate.
3D geometry uses a valid cross-section/projection; exposed surface area excludes shared faces and line-to-plane angle is measured against the projected line.
Area/volume conversions square/cube unit factors; rounded/truncated intervals retain endpoints, and dependent quantities cannot choose incompatible extrema.
Percentage changes multiply successively; reverse change divides by those multipliers. Direct/inverse proportionality includes a fixed constant and correct dimensional scaling.
Histogram frequency is density times width, grouped mean is an estimate using midpoints, and summary statistics must account for frequencies.
Quartiles use cumulative counts and class interpolation; spread/centre comparisons use common measures. Correlation and extrapolation do not establish causality or guaranteed continuation.
Trapezoidal strips use n+1 heights; unequal widths need separate strips. Bias follows chord/curve position, not increasing versus decreasing alone.
Added continuity of the integrand for the elementary fundamental-theorem derivative. Moving lower endpoints reverse the sign; absolute extrema also compare interval endpoints.
Inclusive OR permits both, AND requires both, and a negated strict inequality includes equality. Quantified truth stays within the declared domain;1 is neither prime nor composite.
“A if B” is B=>A, while “A only if B” is A=>B. Iff requires both, and an implication fails only at a true premise and false conclusion.
The contrapositive reverses and negates both clauses and is equivalent; the converse and inverse are not generally equivalent. Valid chains respect direction.
Necessity tests target=>condition; sufficiency tests condition=>target. Counterexamples obey all original assumptions and slope formulas require their nonzero denominators.
Nested witnesses may depend on earlier choices, while one fixed witness is stronger. All/some are interpreted on their stated domains, not an assumed larger set.
Negation changes quantifiers in place and preserves domains; De Morgan rules, implication negation and iff failure cases are correct.
A counterexample satisfies every hypothesis and fails the conclusion; many positive tests do not prove a universal assertion. Sign and primality examples use their definitions.
Even/odd forms2k and2k+1 cover all integers with independent parameters. Direct divisibility proof exhibits a divisor times an integer rather than selected examples.
Cases must exhaust the domain, including boundary/zero/negative cases. Parity proves square residues0or1mod4; absolute values split at every sign-changing argument.
Contradiction retains assumptions while denying the target; rational closure includes only nonzero divisors. A common factor contradicts a rational representation only if lowest terms was required.
Proof dependencies must precede use, symbols must be introduced, and denominators justified. Independently justified lines may be interchangeable.
The first unsupported inference is the error even if the conclusion happens to be true. Circularity, cancellation and squaring each need the stated checks.
Division may discard a zero case and squaring may add roots; equal outputs imply equal inputs only for an injective function on the relevant domain.
Negative multiplication reverses order, zero needs its own case, and |z|>=c for c>0 is a two-interval union. The zero-product rule is specific to zero.
Function height, slope and signed area are distinct; constants change height without slope, stationary zeros need classification, and integral cancellation does not force zero area.
An all-input claim keeps its parameter fixed. A necessary bound needs a sufficiency proof and equality/zero-denominator checks; shared-input extrema may conflict.
A recurrence cycle requires return to the full state, including index phase. Complete blocks and leftovers give distant terms/sums; a nonzero block sum prevents partial sums from cycling.
Pair-avoidance partitions the actual set into distinct valid partner pairs and unmatched values; an extremal avoiding construction plus one extra proves the smallest guarantee.
Necessity and sufficiency are distinct. Odd/even sorted-list median definitions and repeated versus distinct entries determine whether a median must be an entry.
Existential witnesses may depend on earlier variables; a nonconstant real linear map is onto, but zero coefficient needs a separate constant case.
A proof can have a correct conclusion and an invalid inference. Lack of real polynomial factors does not make all integer evaluations prime; cancellation/squaring preserve the stated caveats.
With p disjoint target-sum pairs and s unpaired values, at most p+s can be selected avoiding a pair; when a pair exists one additional choice forces it.
Coefficient convolution adds all products whose exponents reach the target. Evaluating at1 sums a whole coefficient row, not an arbitrary single coefficient.
On0<x<1, x²<x<sqrt(x). Exponential order depends on base. Corrected strict integral comparison to continuous functions on a forward nonempty interval.
Extrema of terms sharing an input cannot be chosen independently. A sum of maxima is only a bound until an attaining common input exists; nested ranges must be propagated.
Equal sine in a triangle allows equal or supplementary angles. A nonsquare inscribed rectangle is a valid irregular counterexample to a regularity claim; symmetry needs justification.
Exactly-one constraints apply to whole statements at shared inputs. Equivalent statements have identical truth values; an apparently sole possibility may still need a consistency construction.
Existence produces a valid candidate; uniqueness eliminates all others. Necessary transformations require reverse checks or substitution, and equal products do not match factors individually.
Remainder cases are exhaustive; divisibility by2and3 combines because coprime, but factors cannot be double-counted. Supplied partner restrictions and prime-equality exceptions are retained.
Useful inputs in identities give simultaneous constraints; antisymmetry cancels only about the right midpoint. A shown period need not be the smallest, and f(-x) reflects zeros.

Parameter degree drops are checked before discriminants. In u=x², positive/zero/negative roots give two/one/no real x-values; a complete quartic-root classification includes distinctness and root signs.
An extremum requires both a universal bound and attainment. Sorted-data totals, circular wrap-around and global distinctness are retained in constructions.
A recurrence invariant is checked under its actual update. Addition/subtraction preserve common divisors; two-term cycles need repeated ordered pairs and parity cycles do not imply numerical cycles.

Whole-function counterexamples meet hypotheses over the entire domain. Added a forward nonempty interval to the continuous nonpositive-integral existence inference; product-root unions remove duplicates.

Event inclusion gives non-strict order, with positive-probability difference needed for strictness. Complements, conditional denominators, independence and swap pairing are applied with their stated assumptions.
